title: Primula nutans Georgi Extract Inhibits Early Adipogenesis Through CHOP-Associated Regulation and Ameliorates Obesity and Insulin Resistance.
authors: Roh, Nayoung; Park, Kyeoungtae; Le, Ducdat; Kim, Eunbin; Dang, Thinhulinh; Dinh, Thientam; Bazarragchaa, Badamtsetseg; Kim, Soo-Yong; Suh, Sung-Suk; Kim, Jung Jin; Lee, Mina; Seo, Jong Bae
one_liner_zh: 该文研究植物提取物抗肥胖作用，仅涉及分子对接预测化合物与代谢调节因子结合，非蛋白质-DNA互作体系，与本课题无关。
abstract: Primula nutans Georgi, a medicinal herb used in Mongolian and Tibetan medicine for treating respiratory ailments, is a natural agent with antiobesity potential. We investigated the antiobesity and insulin-sensitizing effects of P. nutans Georgi extract (PGE) using in vitro and in vivo models. In 3T3-L1 preadipocytes, PGE inhibited adipocyte differentiation and lipid accumulation without cytotoxicity, accompanied by the reduced expression of adipogenic transcription factors (PPARG, C/EBPA, and adiponectin) and lipogenic genes (FASN, SCD1, and ACC), particularly during the early stages of adipogenesis. Similar effects were observed in primary stromal vascular cells derived from mouse inguinal white adipose tissue. PGE upregulated C/EBP homologous protein and C/EBPB and was associated with altered cell cycle progression, increased G2/M phase distribution, and the potential disruption of mitotic clonal expansion during early adipogenesis. In HFD-induced obese mice, intraperitoneal administration of PGE (10 or 30 mg/kg) significantly reduced body weight gain, white adipose tissue mass, and hepatic steatosis, independent of food intake. PGE downregulated lipogenic and proinflammatory gene expression in adipose and hepatic tissues and increased AMPK phosphorylation in white adipose tissue. PGE improved glucose tolerance and was associated with enhanced insulin sensitivity, as evidenced by reduced areas under the curve in the glucose tolerance and insulin tolerance tests and increased circulating adiponectin levels. Feature-based molecular networking identified 61 compounds from PGE. Network pharmacology analysis revealed several antiobesity targets, including PPARG and AKT1. Molecular docking analyses suggested favorable binding affinities between major compounds and metabolic regulators. Collectively, these findings suggest that PGE may suppress adipogenesis and improve metabolic parameters in obese mice, supporting its potential as a natural candidate for obesity and related metabolic disorders.
abstract_zh: Primula nutans Georgi是一种用于蒙古族和藏族医学治疗呼吸系统疾病的药用草本植物，具有抗肥胖潜力的天然药剂。我们利用体外和体内模型研究了P. nutans Georgi提取物（PGE）的抗肥胖和胰岛素增敏作用。在3T3-L1前脂肪细胞中，PGE抑制了脂肪细胞分化和脂质积累，且无细胞毒性，同时伴随脂肪生成转录因子（PPARG、C/EBPA和脂联素）和脂肪生成基因（FASN、SCD1和ACC）表达降低，尤其在脂肪生成的早期阶段。在小鼠腹股沟白色脂肪组织来源的原代基质血管细胞中观察到类似效果。PGE上调了C/EBP同源蛋白和C/EBPB，并与细胞周期进程改变、G2/M期分布增加以及早期脂肪生成过程中有丝分裂克隆扩增的潜在干扰相关。在高脂饮食诱导的肥胖小鼠中，腹腔注射PGE（10或30 mg/kg）显著减少了体重增加、白色脂肪组织质量和肝脏脂肪变性，且与食物摄入无关。PGE下调了脂肪和肝脏组织中脂肪生成和促炎基因的表达，并增加了白色脂肪组织中AMPK的磷酸化。PGE改善了葡萄糖耐量，并与增强的胰岛素敏感性相关，表现为葡萄糖耐量和胰岛素耐量测试中曲线下面积减少以及循环脂联素水平升高。基于特征的分子网络分析从PGE中鉴定出61种化合物。网络药理学分析揭示了多个抗肥胖靶点，包括PPARG和AKT1。分子对接分析表明主要化合物与代谢调节因子之间具有良好的结合亲和力。综合来看，这些发现表明PGE可能抑制脂肪生成并改善肥胖小鼠的代谢参数，支持其作为肥胖及相关代谢紊乱天然候选药物的潜力。
